name: Fairfax House

dates.altered: No.27 remodelled 1760-62, possibly by John Carr for the 9th Viscount Fairfax of Emley; both houses amalgamated and remodelled as a cinema and ballroom in 1920; restored as two houses 1982-84 by Francis Johnson for the York Civic Trust.
dates.note: The node's exemplar gives 1762 and 'Remodelled 1755-62 by John Carr'. The list entry prints 'No.27 c1744, remodelled 1760-62' and attributes the remodelling only as 'possibly by John Carr'. Wikipedia prints 'c. 1744 (No. 27)' and '1760-1762 (No. 27 remodelled)'. All are recorded; none is resolved, and the attribution is not strengthened here.

quotes.text: YORK SE6051NW CASTLEGATE 1112-1/28/141 (North East side) 14/06/54 Nos.25 AND 27 Fairfax House
quotes.page: Official list entry 1259337, Details, entry header

quotes.text: Two houses, now amalgamated. No.27 c1744, remodelled 1760-62; No.25 probably early C19. Both houses amalgamated and remodelled as cinema and ballroom in 1920; restored as two houses 1982-84. No.27 remodelled in C18 possibly by John Carr for the 9th Viscount Fairfax of Emley: C20 restoration by Francis Johnson for the York Civic Trust.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1259337, Details, opening paragraph

quotes.text: MATERIALS: No.27 of orange brick in Flemish bond on stepped plinth of painted stone; painted stone doorcase, quoins and dressings. Rear rebuilt in C19 clamp bricks in English bond. Brick stacks at each side of hipped slate roof.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1259337, Details, MATERIALS paragraph

quotes.text: EXTERIOR: both fronts are 2-storeyed with attics. No.25 has 3 bays; No.27 5 bays, 3 centre bays breaking forward beneath closed pediment.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1259337, Details, EXTERIOR paragraph

quotes.text: Ground floor windows are 12-pane sashes in quoined surrounds with flat arches of stepped voussoirs, over sill band. On first floor, similar windows in plain architraves over sunk panels, have pulvinated friezes, moulded cornices and projecting sills extending as flat sill band. Attic windows are squat 6-pane sashes in plain surrounds with sills.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1259337, Details, EXTERIOR paragraph

quotes.text: Flat band at first floor; moulded cornices beneath attic storey, and to eaves and pediment, beneath plain parapet. Pediment tympanum filled by radial-glazed oculus enclosed in renewed cartouche surround carved with palm fronds.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1259337, Details, EXTERIOR paragraph

quotes.text: No.27 has central pedimented doorcase of attached Doric columns on tall stepped pedestals. Double doors of fielded panels beneath radial fanlight, approached by steps, are recessed in round-arched architrave with moulded impost band.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1259337, Details, EXTERIOR paragraph

measurements.note: Two main storeys with an attic above; the entry names the attic separately and the attic windows are described as squat 6-pane sashes.

measurements.note: No.27 is the Georgian house of the pair. No.25, probably early C19, has 3 bays.
